what: A census of car paint colour on the streets the district is modelled on, by family.
why: docs/BACKLOG.md #91. src/traffic.js and src/streetfurniture.js both draw their chromatic third from a UNIFORM hue wheel while their own comments say the reference is 'overwhelmingly white, silver, grey and black with the occasional red or blue'. The target had never been stated as a table with a source, so this is that table.
source: reference/sarasota/mapillary — Mapillary CC BY-SA 4.0, imagery (c) Mapillary contributors. Reference only; nothing here is traced, sampled or copied into a shipped asset.

method.frame: 2024 panoramas only, one capture campaign, greedily subsampled so no two frames are within 45 m. A pano sees both kerbs, so each frame covers a whole block face.
method.instrument: Visual classification into seven coarse, high-contrast families. NOT a hue measurement: this method can separate white from silver from black from red from blue, and cannot resolve a hue angle. Only cars whose body colour was unambiguous were counted, which in practice means within ~30 m — and that is also what keeps the frames disjoint, since the cars that recur between frames 45 m apart are the distant ones.
method.counted: Parked and moving road vehicles. The capture vehicle itself is excluded.

biases: UNDER-counts chromatic. Dark red and navy read as black in bright Florida midday sun, and only confident calls were counted, so the chromatic share below is a LOWER bound.
OVER-counts white. Four of the vehicles are commercial vans, which are nearly always white and are not passenger cars. The game's traffic fleet is passenger cars.
One season, one week, daytime, dry. Nothing here says anything about a different fleet elsewhere.

frames.note: Main St pedestrianised block, ROAD CLOSED. No vehicles. Kept in the list because a frame with no cars is data about the corridor, and dropping empty frames would bias the per-frame counts.
Side street by the parking decks; only distant vehicles, none confidently readable.
Three of the four white are commercial vans.

families.white: white and off-white, including commercial vans
families.silver: silver, light grey and mid grey
families.black: black, charcoal and any dark body that could not be separated from black

note: `notObserved` is the finding. Zero of the sample fell in any of those families, and four of them are what the shipped uniform hue wheel spends most of its chromatic third on.
